cells.tense: You are standing in a clearing where something fair is already moving back and forth.
cells.act: set the finished thing down in a form that keeps
cells.ask: Put one arrangement that works onto paper — who brings what, how the return arrives — and then let a week pass without touching the page again.
cells.core: There's an exchange in your life that works. You give, something comes back, and neither side keeps score while the thing keeps moving. What holds it up is that the shape is plain: both people can say what they bring. That plainness is doing the labor, and nobody has written it anywhere. Two people being fair shouldn't need one of them standing over it. A clearing with nothing planted still isn't empty. A form is here that hasn't been fixed in place, and fixing it is the work of this hour. Set one working trade down in a shape it can keep while you're gone: the fair arrangement, not a tally of who owes what. Making a thing is not the opposite of keeping it.

cells.tense: You will be bracing for a future where the scales have already tipped against you.
cells.act: carry your own share, all of it
cells.ask: For one week, bring only the parts of an exchange that are yours, then stop each time. If a share of theirs goes uncarried, you'll see it at the week's end.
cells.core: In a clearing where nothing has been planted, you're already hoisting the whole harvest. You bring more than your half, then watch the gap, and bringing turns into waiting for what hasn't come back. The effort is real, but it's aimed at a debt that hasn't happened yet. You're guarding the fairness of a field nobody has planted. A working exchange doesn't need a guard at every edge. This week, bring only what is yours, and leave the other portions unaccounted. Not because their side doesn't matter, but because a process that runs doesn't need you auditing it hourly. What you actually owe is your own share, all of it, without the ledger. Anything missing will show itself on Friday without you checking every mile.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that shut behind you before this clearing had a name.
cells.act: sort what matters from what does not, carefully
cells.ask: Take one exchange as it actually went and mark what genuinely moved it forward against what only felt like fairness. Then cross off one item from the second list and stop bringing it.
cells.core: In this clearing, something is missing. You bring, and nothing lands — no return arrives, and the ground stays as bare as it was. The seed has everything in it and nothing has come up. The way back starts with telling things apart, not with more force: take one exchange as it actually went and mark what genuinely moved it forward against what only felt fair. Then cross one item off the second list and stop bringing it. Not to withhold from anyone — just to clear some ground so what's real has room. What remains still stands. Tend that and nothing else for a week, and notice what the shorter list leaves open.

cells.tense: The pen is down in a clearing you're already writing in, and you haven't claimed the writing.
cells.act: pause before you let it be known
cells.ask: Next time a fair split is on the table, hold your own read of it for ten minutes before you say anything. Then act, and let the ten minutes be all the ceremony.
cells.core: Somewhere in you a fair answer about an exchange has already arrived. You act on it — you even the thing out, take the smaller half, offer before being asked — and your account of it says that's just how you are. In a clearing where everything is still possible, the deciding is already being done by a hand you're calling the room. The read is real, and it lands without argument, then goes unclaimed. It isn't scorekeeping; it's the kind of perception that arrives before speech. Next time a fair split is on the table, hold your own read of it for ten minutes before you move. Held that long, it turns into something you can use rather than a fact of your character. Say it, or don't. It stays yours either way.

A reader could reasonably say the readings assume a live situation with another person when the draw might be about exchanges still unformed in a seed seat. The asks survive: they are acts the medicine does in a week, needing no one else, and they teach something even if the read misses the person. The sentence that serves me more than them is 'you are a vessel of justice' — cut. Also cut any plain 'before you give' framing in Too Little: a Past-anchored cell that locates the person must not say what happened or what it cost, so the ask stays an act, not a story about the past.

attempts.check: The record hands me acts, a mechanism, and a seed seat, but nothing about who this person trades with or what has already passed between them, so every scene in the second person is mine, not the record's. A reader could fairly say I let the clearing do more work than the draw does; the asks survive that, since each is a week-sized act the medicine performs, needs no one else, and teaches something even if my read misses. The lines that served me more than them were anything certifying the person's past accuracy and anything noun-shaped built out of a verb; both are gone. The four asks now take four different shapes: an unbounded noticing, a week-long practice with a stop built in, a bounded crossing-off, a ten-minute hold.
